trimethyltin chloride (a known neurotoxicant) induces a high frequency of Ml cells in human peripheral blood mononuclear lymphocytes, which is associated with a delay in cell division, cell cycle kinetics and DNA synthesis in aged lymphocytes.
trimethyltin chloride induced an increase in the duration of DNA synthesis in human lymphocytes, especially in aged lymphocytes.
the trimethyltin chloride induced the age-related suppression of the cell division and cell cycles in human peripheral blood cells.

the effect of trimethyltin chloride (C3H5SnCl3) on cell division and cell kinetics in human peripheral lymphocytes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the trimethyltin chloride induced alterations in cell division, cell cycle kinetics and DNA synthesis in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells are age-related and dose-dependent.

trimethyltin chloride induced a significant increase in the number of M1 (1st metaphase) cells in lymphocytes of human donors of 40–70 age group, which may indicate a longer DNA synthesis in the cell cycle.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trimethyltin chloride induced a significant decrease in the mitotic index in human lymphocytes and this decrease was age-dependent.
trimethyltin chloride induced a delay in the cell cycle of lymphocytes, which may indicate a longer period of DNA synthesis.
trimethyltin chloride induced an age-related delay in DNA synthesis in cultured peripheral blood lymphocytes of human donors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trimethyltin chloride is an age-associated suppressant of cell division and the duration of DNA synthesis in cultured human lymphocytes.
the age-related suppression of mitotic index and cell cycle kinetics is more pronounced in trimethyltin-treated cultures of aged lymphocytes.
the age-dependent alterations in cell division are not due to a direct effect of trimethyltin chloride on the lymphocytes, as these alterations are also seen in untreated aged lymphocytes.
